description: Volcanoes question bank derived exhaustively from Volcanoes.pdf. Every syllabus point, definition, classification, example, exam trap and revision fact converted to unique MCQs. Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: What is a volcano?

options.A: A mountain made only of folded sedimentary rock
options.B: An opening, vent or connected system of fractures in Earth's crust through which magma, gases and volcanic materials erupt or have erupted onto the surface
options.C: A deep ocean trench formed by plate subduction
options.D: A depression formed by glacial erosion

questions.explanation: A volcano is an opening, vent or connected system of fractures in Earth's crust through which magma, gases and volcanic materials erupt or have erupted onto the surface; accumulated products may build a volcanic landform.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: What is volcanism?

options.A: Only the eruption of lava at the surface
options.B: The movement of magma from within Earth into the crust or onto the surface, together with release of volcanic gases and solid fragments, including both intrusive and extrusive activity
options.C: The weathering of volcanic rock by wind
options.D: The formation of coral reefs around volcanic islands

questions.explanation: Volcanism includes intrusive activity below the surface and extrusive activity at the surface, together with release of gases and solid fragments.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: What causes volcanic activity?

options.A: Only the addition of water to rocks
options.B: Molten or partially molten rock forming in the mantle or crust, rising because of buoyancy and pressure, and finding pathways through fractures or conduits
options.C: Only the cooling of the Earth's core
options.D: Only meteorite impacts

questions.explanation: Volcanic activity occurs when molten or partially molten rock forms in the mantle or crust, rises due to buoyancy and pressure, and finds pathways through fractures or conduits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: Which processes can generate magma?

options.A: Only heat transfer
options.B: Decompression melting, addition of water and other volatiles, and heat transfer
options.C: Only addition of water
options.D: Only radioactive decay

questions.explanation: Decompression melting, addition of water and other volatiles, and heat transfer can generate magma.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: What are the principal tectonic settings in which volcanoes form?

options.A: Only divergent plate boundaries
options.B: Only convergent plate boundaries
options.C: Divergent plate boundaries, convergent plate boundaries and intraplate hotspots
options.D: Only intraplate hotspots

questions.explanation: Divergent boundaries, convergent boundaries and intraplate hotspots are the principal settings; volcanism also occurs in some continental rifts and zones of crustal weakness.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: How does volcanism occur at divergent plate boundaries?

options.A: Water released from a descending plate melts the mantle wedge
options.B: Hot mantle rises as plates move apart and pressure decreases, causing decompression melting that produces magma erupting along mid-ocean ridges or continental rifts
options.C: A mantle plume burns through a moving plate
options.D: Friction between colliding plates melts the crust

questions.explanation: As plates move apart, hot mantle rises and pressure decreases; decompression causes partial melting, producing magma that erupts along mid-ocean ridges or continental rifts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: How does volcanism occur at convergent plate boundaries?

options.A: Plates move apart and mantle decompresses
options.B: Water and other volatiles released from the descending plate promote melting in the mantle wedge above it, and magma rises to produce volcanic arcs
options.C: A hotspot burns through the plate
options.D: The crust is stretched and thinned

questions.explanation: At subduction zones, volatiles from the descending plate promote melting in the mantle wedge, producing volcanic arcs commonly containing composite volcanoes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: What is hotspot volcanism?

options.A: Volcanism caused only by subduction
options.B: Volcanism where unusually hot mantle material or focused mantle upwelling produces melting beneath a moving plate, forming volcanic chains such as the Hawaiian Islands
options.C: Volcanism caused by continental collision
options.D: Volcanism caused by glacial melting

questions.explanation: Hotspot volcanism occurs where unusually hot mantle material or focused upwelling produces melting beneath a moving plate, forming chains like Hawaii. Origins and plume structures remain research subjects.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: Are all volcanoes located at plate boundaries?

options.A: Yes, without exception
options.B: No; some form within plates above hotspots, such as Hawaii and Yellowstone
options.C: Yes, but only at divergent boundaries
options.D: No; all volcanoes form at hotspots

questions.explanation: Many volcanoes occur at plate boundaries, but some form within plates above hotspots, such as Hawaii and Yellowstone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Meaning and Causes of Volcanic Activity
questions.question: What is the difference between intrusive and extrusive igneous activity?

options.A: Intrusive activity occurs at the surface; extrusive activity occurs underground
options.B: Intrusive activity occurs when magma cools and solidifies beneath the surface forming dykes, sills, batholiths and laccoliths; extrusive activity occurs when lava or fragmented material erupts at the surface and cools there
options.C: Both occur only at the surface
options.D: Intrusive activity only forms volcanic cones

questions.explanation: Intrusive activity forms bodies such as dykes, sills, batholiths and laccoliths below the surface; extrusive activity occurs when lava or fragmented material erupts and cools at the surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is magma?

options.A: Molten rock that has erupted onto Earth's surface
options.B: Molten or partially molten rock beneath Earth's surface, commonly containing liquid melt, crystals and dissolved gases
options.C: Fine rock fragments ejected into the air
options.D: A type of sedimentary rock

questions.explanation: Magma is molten or partially molten rock beneath Earth's surface, commonly containing liquid melt, crystals and dissolved gases.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is lava?

options.A: Molten rock beneath the surface
options.B: Magma that has reached and erupted onto Earth's surface, forming volcanic rocks as it cools
options.C: Dissolved gases in magma
options.D: Fragmented volcanic material ejected into the air

questions.explanation: Lava is magma that has reached and erupted onto Earth's surface; as it cools and solidifies it forms volcanic rocks.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main difference between magma and lava?

options.A: Magma is at the surface; lava is below the surface
options.B: Magma is below the surface; lava is magma at the surface after eruption
options.C: They are identical in all respects
options.D: Lava contains no gases, but magma does

questions.explanation: Magma is below the surface; lava is magma at the surface after eruption.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are volcanic gases?

options.A: Gases produced only by burning vegetation
options.B: Gases dissolved in magma or released from it; water vapour is commonly most abundant, with carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide also important
options.C: Gases found only in the atmosphere
options.D: Gases released only by weathering of basalt

questions.explanation: Volcanic gases are dissolved in magma or released from it; water vapour is commonly most abundant, while carbon dioxide and sulphur dioxide are also important.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is tephra?

options.A: Only fine volcanic ash
options.B: The general term for all fragments of volcanic material ejected into the air during an eruption, regardless of size
options.C: Molten rock flowing at the surface
options.D: A type of intrusive igneous body

questions.explanation: Tephra is the general term for all fragments of volcanic material ejected into the air during an eruption; fine ash, lapilli, blocks and bombs are examples.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is volcanic ash?

options.A: Soft ash produced by burning wood
options.B: Fragments of volcanic glass, minerals and rock smaller than 2 millimetres; abrasive rock material, not combustion ash
options.C: Large molten fragments larger than 64 mm
options.D: A type of lava flow

questions.explanation: Volcanic ash consists of fragments of volcanic glass, minerals and rock smaller than 2 mm; it is abrasive rock material, not the soft ash from burning wood.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between lava and pyroclastic material?

options.A: Lava consists of fragmented particles; pyroclastic material is molten rock
options.B: Lava is molten rock flowing or spreading at the surface; pyroclastic material consists of fragmented volcanic particles such as ash, lapilli, blocks and bombs ejected during explosive activity
options.C: Both are identical
options.D: Pyroclastic material is found only underground

questions.explanation: Lava is molten rock flowing or spreading at the surface, whereas pyroclastic material consists of fragmented volcanic particles ejected during explosive activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is magma viscosity?

options.A: The temperature of magma
options.B: A fluid's resistance to flow; high-viscosity magma is thick and flows less easily, low-viscosity magma is more fluid and can travel farther
options.C: The gas content of magma
options.D: The colour of magma

questions.explanation: Viscosity is a fluid's resistance to flow; high-viscosity magma is thick and flows less easily, while low-viscosity magma is more fluid and travels farther.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How does silica content affect magma viscosity?

options.A: Higher silica produces lower viscosity
options.B: In general, higher silica content produces more polymerised melt structures and higher viscosity; basaltic magma is relatively low in silica and fluid, rhyolitic magma is high in silica and highly viscous
options.C: Silica content has no effect on viscosity
options.D: Lower silica always produces explosive eruptions

questions.explanation: Higher silica produces more polymerised melt structures and higher viscosity; basaltic magma is usually low in silica and fluid, rhyolitic magma is high in silica and highly viscous. Temperature and crystal and gas content also affect viscosity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the typical composition and eruption tendency of basaltic magma?

options.A: High silica, highly viscous, often explosive
options.B: Lower silica, generally hotter and less viscous, often effusive with extensive lava flows and shield volcanoes
options.C: Intermediate silica, always explosive
options.D: No silica, always forms lava domes

questions.explanation: Basaltic magma is lower in silica, generally hotter and less viscous, and often effusive, producing extensive lava flows and shield volcanoes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the typical composition and eruption tendency of andesitic magma?

options.A: Lower silica, always effusive
options.B: Intermediate silica and viscosity; can produce both lava flows and explosive eruptions, common in volcanic arcs
options.C: High silica, always effusive
options.D: No silica, only forms cinder cones

questions.explanation: Andesitic magma has intermediate silica and viscosity and can produce both lava flows and explosive eruptions; it is common in volcanic arcs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the typical composition and eruption tendency of rhyolitic magma?

options.A: Lower silica, generally hotter, always effusive
options.B: High silica, generally cooler and highly viscous, often explosive producing ash, pumice, domes and pyroclastic flows
options.C: Intermediate silica, only produces lava plateaus
options.D: No silica, only produces cinder cones

questions.explanation: Rhyolitic magma is high in silica, generally cooler and highly viscous, and often explosive, producing ash, pumice, domes and pyroclastic flows.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Causes and Styles of Volcanic Eruptions
questions.question: What is an effusive eruption?

options.A: An eruption dominated by explosive ejection of ash and pumice
options.B: An eruption dominated by relatively steady outpouring of lava, often because magma is sufficiently fluid and gas can escape without a major explosion
options.C: An eruption that produces only pyroclastic flows
options.D: An eruption that produces only lahars

questions.explanation: An effusive eruption is dominated by relatively steady outpouring of lava, often because magma is sufficiently fluid and gas can escape without a major explosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Causes and Styles of Volcanic Eruptions
questions.question: What is an explosive eruption?

options.A: An eruption dominated by steady lava outpouring
options.B: An eruption where expanding gases fragment magma and eject ash, pumice, blocks and other material at high speed, producing ash columns, pyroclastic density currents and widespread tephra deposits
options.C: An eruption that produces only lava plateaus
options.D: An eruption that produces only volcanic plugs

questions.explanation: In an explosive eruption, expanding gases fragment magma and eject ash, pumice, blocks and other material at high speed; it can produce ash columns, pyroclastic density currents and widespread tephra deposits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Causes and Styles of Volcanic Eruptions
questions.question: What is a pyroclastic flow or density current?

options.A: A slow-moving river of lava
options.B: A fast-moving, ground-hugging current of hot gas, ash and volcanic fragments that moves down a volcano's slopes and across surrounding terrain; among the most dangerous volcanic hazards
options.C: A mudflow made of water mixed with volcanic ash
options.D: A type of intrusive igneous body

questions.explanation: A pyroclastic flow or density current is a fast-moving, ground-hugging current of hot gas, ash and volcanic fragments moving down slopes and across terrain; it is among the most dangerous volcanic hazards.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Causes and Styles of Volcanic Eruptions
questions.question: What is a lahar?

options.A: A fast-moving current of hot gas and ash
options.B: A volcanic mudflow or debris flow made of water mixed with volcanic ash, soil and rock fragments; can travel rapidly down valleys and river channels, sometimes long after an eruption
options.C: A large fragment of molten lava ejected during an eruption
options.D: A highly vesicular volcanic rock that can float on water

questions.explanation: A lahar is a volcanic mudflow or debris flow made of water mixed with volcanic ash, soil and rock fragments; it can travel rapidly down valleys and river channels, sometimes long after an eruption.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Causes and Styles of Volcanic Eruptions
questions.question: What is a volcanic bomb?

options.A: A fine ash particle smaller than 2 mm
options.B: A large fragment of molten or semi-molten lava ejected during an eruption that solidifies while travelling through the air; generally larger than 64 mm in standard size classification
options.C: A mudflow of volcanic ash and water
options.D: A type of intrusive igneous body

questions.explanation: A volcanic bomb is a large fragment of molten or semi-molten lava ejected during an eruption that solidifies while travelling through the air; in standard size classification it is generally larger than 64 mm.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Causes and Styles of Volcanic Eruptions
questions.question: What is pumice?

options.A: A dark, dense basaltic rock
options.B: A highly vesicular volcanic rock formed when gas-rich, usually silica-rich magma cools rapidly; its abundant cavities can make it light enough to float on water
options.C: A type of volcanic mudflow
options.D: A large fragment of molten lava that solidifies in air

questions.explanation: Pumice is a highly vesicular volcanic rock formed when gas-rich, usually silica-rich magma cools rapidly; its abundant cavities can make it light enough to float on water.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Causes and Styles of Volcanic Eruptions
questions.question: What is scoria?

options.A: A light-coloured rock that floats on water
options.B: A dark, vesicular volcanic rock, commonly basaltic or andesitic, with many gas cavities, generally denser than pumice
options.C: A type of volcanic ash smaller than 2 mm
options.D: A mudflow of volcanic ash and water

questions.explanation: Scoria is a dark, vesicular volcanic rock, commonly basaltic or andesitic, with many gas cavities; it is generally denser than pumice.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an active volcano?

options.A: A volcano that has never erupted
options.B: A volcano that is erupting now, has erupted in recent geological or historical time, or shows evidence of activity and is considered capable of erupting again
options.C: A volcano that will certainly never erupt again
options.D: A volcano that is always dormant

questions.explanation: An active volcano is one that is erupting now, has erupted in recent geological or historical time, or shows evidence of activity and is considered capable of erupting again; the exact time criterion varies among organisations.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a dormant volcano?

options.A: A volcano that has no magma system
options.B: A volcano that is not currently erupting and may have remained quiet for a long period but has the potential to erupt again
options.C: A volcano that will certainly never erupt again
options.D: A volcano that is always erupting

questions.explanation: A dormant volcano is not currently erupting and may have remained quiet for a long period, but has the potential to erupt again.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is an extinct volcano?

options.A: A volcano that erupts every year
options.B: A volcano not expected to erupt again because its magma supply or volcanic system is considered inactive
options.C: A volcano that is currently erupting
options.D: A volcano with a confirmed future eruption date

questions.explanation: An extinct volcano is one not expected to erupt again because its magma supply or volcanic system is considered inactive; this classification can be uncertain because volcanic systems may have very long repose periods.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Is there one universal time limit separating active, dormant and extinct volcanoes?

options.A: Yes, 100 years for all agencies
options.B: No; definitions vary between agencies and textbooks, and classification depends on eruption history, geological setting, signs of unrest and assessment of whether it may erupt again
options.C: Yes, 10,000 years for all agencies
options.D: Yes, 1,000 years for all agencies

questions.explanation: No universal time limit exists; definitions vary between agencies and textbooks, and classification depends on eruption history, geological setting, signs of unrest and assessment of whether it may erupt again.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Can a dormant volcano become active again?

options.A: No, dormancy is permanent
options.B: Yes; dormancy means a period of inactivity, not permanent extinction, and a dormant volcano can erupt again if its magmatic system becomes active
options.C: Only if it is located at a divergent boundary
options.D: Only if it is classified as extinct first

questions.explanation: Dormancy means a period of inactivity, not permanent extinction; a dormant volcano can erupt again if its magmatic system becomes active.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Can an extinct volcano be identified with absolute certainty?

options.A: Yes, always
options.B: Not always; volcanic systems have different lifespans, and a long period without eruption does not alone prove extinction; classifications are based on geological evidence and the state of the volcanic system
options.C: Yes, if it has been quiet for 100 years
options.D: Yes, if it is located in Iceland

questions.explanation: Extinct status cannot always be identified with absolute certainty; volcanic systems have different lifespans, and a long period without eruption does not alone prove extinction. Classifications are based on geological evidence and the state of the volcanic system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an active volcano in India?

options.A: Narcondam
options.B: Barren Island
options.C: Deccan Traps
options.D: Dhindohar

questions.explanation: Barren Island in the Andaman Sea is India's only confirmed historically active volcano. Narcondam is generally described as dormant or inactive.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is Mount Fuji sometimes described as dormant but sometimes classified as active?

options.A: Because it is located at a divergent boundary
options.B: Because simplified textbooks may call it dormant, but scientific catalogues may classify it as active because it has erupted in the Holocene
options.C: Because it has never erupted
options.D: Because it is located in India

questions.explanation: Mount Fuji is often called dormant in simplified textbooks, but scientific catalogues may classify it as active because it has erupted in the Holocene. Active/dormant/extinct labels are not unchanging facts.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a shield volcano?

options.A: A steep-sided cone built of alternating lava and ash layers
options.B: A broad, gently sloping volcanic mountain built mainly by repeated flows of fluid, usually basaltic lava, resembling a warrior's shield lying on the ground
options.C: A small, steep cone of loose pyroclastic fragments
options.D: A large collapse depression formed after magma withdrawal

questions.explanation: A shield volcano is a broad, gently sloping volcanic mountain built mainly by repeated flows of fluid, usually basaltic lava; its profile resembles a warrior's shield lying on the ground.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are shield volcanoes formed?

options.A: Explosive bursts eject molten fragments that fall around a vent
options.B: Low-viscosity lava erupts from a central vent or flank fissures and spreads over wide areas; repeated flows accumulate in thin layers and gradually build a large, broad volcanic edifice
options.C: Alternating layers of lava and pyroclastic material build a steep cone
options.D: A magma reservoir collapses along ring faults

questions.explanation: Low-viscosity lava erupts from a central vent or flank fissures and spreads over wide areas; repeated flows accumulate in thin layers and gradually build a large, broad volcanic edifice.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the characteristics of shield volcanoes?

options.A: Steep slopes, layered structure, mainly andesitic magma
options.B: Broad bases, gentle slopes, extensive lava flows, commonly basaltic compositions and generally effusive eruption styles; they can grow to very large sizes
options.C: Small size, steep slopes, made mainly of loose pyroclastic fragments
options.D: Formed only by collapse of a magma reservoir

questions.explanation: Shield volcanoes have broad bases, gentle slopes, extensive lava flows, commonly basaltic compositions and generally effusive eruption styles; they can grow to very large sizes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are well-known shield volcanoes?

options.A: Mount Fuji and Mount Vesuvius
options.B: Mauna Loa and Kilauea in Hawaii
options.C: Paricutin and Sunset Crater
options.D: Mount St. Helens and Mount Pinatubo

questions.explanation: Mauna Loa and Kilauea in Hawaii are well-known shield volcanoes; Mauna Loa is among the largest active shield volcanoes on Earth.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a composite volcano (stratovolcano)?

options.A: A broad, gently sloping dome built only of fluid lava flows
options.B: A steep-sided volcanic cone built from alternating layers of lava flows and fragmented material such as ash, cinders and pyroclastic deposits
options.C: A small cone made only of loose cinders and scoria
options.D: A long crack in the crust from which lava emerges

questions.explanation: A composite volcano, or stratovolcano, is a steep-sided volcanic cone built from alternating layers of lava flows and fragmented material such as ash, cinders and pyroclastic deposits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are composite volcanoes formed?

options.A: Low-viscosity lava spreads over wide areas in thin layers
options.B: Repeated eruptions deposit lava and pyroclastic material around a central vent and associated vents; alternating deposits build a high, steep volcanic cone over many eruptions
options.C: A single explosive burst ejects fragments that fall around a vent
options.D: A magma reservoir collapses along ring faults

questions.explanation: Repeated eruptions deposit lava and pyroclastic material around a central vent and associated vents; alternating deposits build a high, steep volcanic cone over many eruptions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the characteristics of composite volcanoes?

options.A: Broad, gently sloping, built only of basalt
options.B: Often steep-sided and relatively symmetrical, with layered structures; may produce both lava flows and explosive eruptions; magma is commonly andesitic to dacitic, although compositions vary
options.C: Small, steep cones made largely of loose pyroclastic fragments
options.D: Long cracks in the crust rather than a central vent

questions.explanation: Composite volcanoes are often steep-sided and relatively symmetrical, have layered structures, and may produce both lava flows and explosive eruptions; their magma is commonly andesitic to dacitic, although compositions vary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of composite volcanoes?

options.A: Mauna Loa and Kilauea
options.B: Mount Fuji, Mount Vesuvius, Mount St. Helens, Mount Cotopaxi, Mount Pinatubo and Mount Mayon
options.C: Paricutin and Sunset Crater
options.D: Laki and the Deccan Traps

questions.explanation: Mount Fuji (Japan), Mount Vesuvius (Italy), Mount St. Helens (USA), Mount Cotopaxi (Ecuador), Mount Pinatubo and Mount Mayon (Philippines) are examples of composite volcanoes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cinder cone volcano?

options.A: A broad, gently sloping dome built of fluid lava flows
options.B: A relatively small, steep-sided cone formed when fragments of gas-rich lava, such as cinders and scoria, fall and accumulate around a volcanic vent
options.C: A steep-sided cone built of alternating lava and pyroclastic layers
options.D: A large collapse depression formed after magma withdrawal

questions.explanation: A cinder cone is a relatively small, steep-sided cone formed when fragments of gas-rich lava, such as cinders and scoria, fall and accumulate around a volcanic vent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are cinder cones formed?

options.A: Low-viscosity lava spreads over wide areas in thin layers
options.B: Explosive bursts eject molten fragments into the air; the fragments cool, fall around the vent and accumulate to form a cone, commonly with a bowl-shaped summit crater; lava flows may also issue from the base or flank
options.C: Alternating layers of lava and pyroclastic material build a steep cone
options.D: A magma reservoir collapses along ring faults

questions.explanation: Explosive bursts eject molten fragments into the air; the fragments cool, fall around the vent and accumulate to form a cone, commonly with a bowl-shaped summit crater. Lava flows may also issue from the base or flank.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the characteristics of cinder cones?

options.A: Broad bases, gentle slopes, extensive lava flows
options.B: Usually smaller than shield and composite volcanoes, steep slopes, consisting mainly of loose or partly consolidated pyroclastic fragments, commonly possessing a summit crater
options.C: Steep-sided, layered structure, andesitic to dacitic magma
options.D: Formed only along long cracks in the crust

questions.explanation: Cinder cones are usually smaller than shield and composite volcanoes, have steep slopes, consist mainly of loose or partly consolidated pyroclastic fragments and commonly possess a summit crater.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are classic examples of cinder cones?

options.A: Mauna Loa and Kilauea
options.B: Mount Fuji and Mount Vesuvius
options.C: Paricutin in Mexico and Sunset Crater in Arizona, United States
options.D: Laki and the Deccan Traps

questions.explanation: Paricutin in Mexico is a classic example of a cinder cone; Sunset Crater in Arizona, United States, is another well-known cinder cone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a fissure eruption?

options.A: An eruption from a single central vent building a steep cone
options.B: A volcanic eruption in which lava emerges from long cracks or fractures in the Earth's crust rather than from a single central volcanic vent
options.C: An eruption that produces only pyroclastic flows
options.D: An eruption that occurs only at hotspots

questions.explanation: A fissure eruption is a volcanic eruption in which lava emerges from long cracks or fractures in the Earth's crust rather than from a single central volcanic vent.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How do fissure eruptions occur?

options.A: Magma rises through a single circular conduit and builds a steep cone
options.B: Magma rises through an elongated fracture or series of cracks; lava may issue along an extended line, spread over broad areas and form extensive lava fields or plateaus
options.C: A magma reservoir collapses along ring faults
options.D: Explosive bursts eject fragments that fall around a vent

questions.explanation: Magma rises through an elongated fracture or series of cracks; lava may issue along an extended line, spread over broad areas and form extensive lava fields or plateaus.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What type of lava commonly occurs in large fissure eruptions?

options.A: Rhyolitic lava, because it is highly viscous
options.B: Basaltic lava, because its low viscosity allows it to flow over large distances, although eruption compositions can vary
options.C: Andesitic lava only
options.D: No lava occurs in fissure eruptions

questions.explanation: Basaltic lava is common in large fissure eruptions because its low viscosity allows it to flow over large distances, although eruption compositions can vary.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of fissure eruptions?

options.A: Mauna Loa and Kilauea
options.B: The Deccan Traps of India and the Laki fissure eruption in Iceland in 1783–1784
options.C: Paricutin and Sunset Crater
options.D: Mount Fuji and Mount Vesuvius

questions.explanation: The Deccan Traps of India were produced by enormous episodes of flood-basalt volcanism involving fissure-fed eruptions; the Laki fissure eruption in Iceland in 1783–1784 is a famous historical example.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Are fissure eruptions the same as shield volcanoes?

options.A: Yes, they are identical
options.B: No; a shield volcano is a broad volcanic edifice built mainly by repeated lava flows, while a fissure eruption describes the geometry of the eruptive opening and may produce extensive lava sheets or plateaus
options.C: Yes, both form only at hotspots
options.D: No; fissure eruptions form only cinder cones

questions.explanation: A shield volcano is a broad volcanic edifice built mainly by repeated lava flows; a fissure eruption describes the geometry of the eruptive opening and may produce extensive lava sheets or plateaus.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are volcanic landforms?

options.A: Only surface features formed by erosion
options.B: Surface features formed by the eruption, accumulation, cooling and solidification of lava and pyroclastic material, or by the collapse and erosion of volcanic structures
options.C: Only underground igneous bodies
options.D: Only features formed by glaciers

questions.explanation: Volcanic landforms are surface features formed by the eruption, accumulation, cooling and solidification of lava and pyroclastic material, or by the collapse and erosion of volcanic structures.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are volcanic landforms classified?

options.A: Only as extrusive landforms
options.B: As extrusive landforms formed at the surface (cones, craters, calderas, lava plateaus, volcanic islands) and intrusive landforms formed when magma solidifies below the surface (dykes, sills, batholiths, laccoliths, volcanic plugs)
options.C: Only as intrusive landforms
options.D: Only by their colour

questions.explanation: Volcanic landforms may be classified as extrusive landforms formed at the surface (such as cones, craters, calderas, lava plateaus and volcanic islands) and intrusive landforms formed when magma solidifies below the surface (such as dykes, sills, batholiths, laccoliths and volcanic plugs).

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a volcanic mountain?

options.A: A mountain formed only by folding
options.B: An elevated landform built mainly by the accumulation of lava, ash and other volcanic products around a vent or along fissures
options.C: A depression formed by collapse
options.D: A long crack in the crust

questions.explanation: A volcanic mountain is an elevated landform built mainly by the accumulation of lava, ash and other volcanic products around a vent or along fissures.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How are volcanic mountains formed?

options.A: By glacial deposition
options.B: Repeated eruptions deposit lava and fragmented material; as successive deposits accumulate and solidify, they build a volcanic cone or broad volcanic edifice
options.C: By the collapse of a magma reservoir
options.D: By the erosion of sedimentary layers

questions.explanation: Repeated eruptions deposit lava and fragmented material; as successive deposits accumulate and solidify, they build a volcanic cone or broad volcanic edifice.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Are all volcanic mountains steep cones?

options.A: Yes, all volcanic mountains are steep cones
options.B: No; shield volcanoes are broad and gently sloping, composite volcanoes are often steep, and some volcanic mountains have complex or irregular shapes; erosion and collapse can also modify their original form
options.C: No; all volcanic mountains are broad and gentle
options.D: Yes, all volcanic mountains are irregular in shape

questions.explanation: Not all volcanic mountains are steep cones; shield volcanoes are broad and gently sloping, composite volcanoes are often steep, and some volcanic mountains have complex or irregular shapes. Erosion and collapse can also modify their original form.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a lava plateau?

options.A: A steep-sided cone built of alternating lava and ash
options.B: A broad, elevated region formed by repeated outpouring of fluid lava, commonly basaltic, from fissures; successive flows spread over large areas and solidify in layers
options.C: A large collapse depression formed after magma withdrawal
options.D: A small bowl-shaped depression around a vent

questions.explanation: A lava plateau is a broad, elevated region formed by repeated outpouring of fluid lava, commonly basaltic, from fissures; successive flows spread over large areas and solidify in layers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How is a lava plateau formed?

options.A: A single explosive eruption ejects ash that falls around a vent
options.B: Large volumes of fluid lava erupt through fissures or multiple vents, spread across extensive areas and cool; repeated eruptions stack successive lava sheets, creating a thick, wide plateau
options.C: A magma reservoir collapses along ring faults
options.D: Glaciers deposit rock debris over a broad area

questions.explanation: Large volumes of fluid lava erupt through fissures or multiple vents, spread across extensive areas and cool; repeated eruptions stack successive lava sheets, creating a thick, wide plateau.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are flood basalts?

options.A: Small cinder cones formed by explosive bursts
options.B: Very large accumulations of basaltic lava produced by extensive eruptions, often through fissure systems, over geologically short intervals
options.C: Steep-sided composite volcanoes
options.D: Large collapse depressions at volcanoes

questions.explanation: Flood basalts are very large accumulations of basaltic lava produced by extensive eruptions, often through fissure systems, over geologically short intervals.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the volcanic significance of the Deccan Plateau?

options.A: It is a currently active composite volcano
options.B: The Deccan Traps in western and central India are a major flood-basalt province formed by enormous volcanic eruptions near the end of the Cretaceous Period, around the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary; an important example of plateau basalt
options.C: It is a small cinder cone in the Andaman Sea
options.D: It is a large caldera formed after magma withdrawal

questions.explanation: The Deccan Traps in western and central India are a major flood-basalt province formed by enormous volcanic eruptions near the end of the Cretaceous Period, around the Cretaceous–Paleogene boundary; they are an important example of plateau basalt.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of large igneous provinces or lava plateaus?

options.A: Mount Fuji and Mount Vesuvius
options.B: The Siberian Traps in Russia, the Columbia River Basalt Group in the northwestern United States, and the Paraná–Etendeka flood-basalt province in South America and Africa
options.C: Paricutin and Sunset Crater
options.D: Barren Island and Narcondam

questions.explanation: The Siberian Traps in Russia, the Columbia River Basalt Group in the northwestern United States and the Paraná–Etendeka flood-basalt province in South America and Africa are examples of large igneous provinces or lava plateaus.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a volcanic crater?

options.A: A large basin-shaped depression formed mainly by collapse of a volcanic edifice
options.B: A relatively small, usually circular or bowl-shaped depression around a volcanic vent, formed through explosive excavation, collapse of material around a vent, or accumulation and modification of erupted deposits
options.C: A long crack in the crust from which lava emerges
options.D: A steep-sided mound formed by viscous lava

questions.explanation: A crater is a relatively small, usually circular or bowl-shaped depression around a volcanic vent; it may form through explosive excavation, collapse of material around a vent, or accumulation and modification of erupted deposits.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Where is a crater usually located?

options.A: Only at the base of a volcano
options.B: Commonly near the summit of a volcanic cone, although craters can also occur on the flanks or around subsidiary vents
options.C: Only in ocean trenches
options.D: Only in continental rifts

questions.explanation: A crater is commonly found near the summit of a volcanic cone, although craters can also occur on the flanks or around subsidiary vents.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Is a crater the same as a caldera?

options.A: Yes, they are identical
options.B: No; a crater is generally smaller and closely associated with a vent, while a caldera is a much larger depression formed mainly by collapse of a volcanic edifice after substantial magma withdrawal
options.C: Yes, both form only by explosive excavation
options.D: No; a crater is always larger than a caldera

questions.explanation: A crater is generally smaller and closely associated with a vent; a caldera is a much larger depression formed mainly by collapse of a volcanic edifice after substantial magma withdrawal, although other collapse processes can contribute.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a caldera?

options.A: A small bowl-shaped depression around a vent
options.B: A large basin-shaped volcanic depression formed when the roof of a magma reservoir or a substantial part of a volcanic edifice collapses, commonly after a large volume of magma has been erupted or withdrawn
options.C: A steep-sided mound formed by viscous lava
options.D: A sheet-like intrusive body parallel to rock layers

questions.explanation: A caldera is a large basin-shaped volcanic depression formed when the roof of a magma reservoir or a substantial part of a volcanic edifice collapses, commonly after a large volume of magma has been erupted or withdrawn.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: How is a caldera formed?

options.A: A single explosive burst excavates a small bowl-shaped depression
options.B: A major eruption or magma withdrawal can leave a partially emptied reservoir; the overlying rock loses support and collapses along ring faults, creating a large depression; later eruptions, lakes or sedimentation may modify the caldera
options.C: Low-viscosity lava spreads over wide areas in thin layers
options.D: Explosive bursts eject fragments that fall around a vent

questions.explanation: A major eruption or magma withdrawal can leave a partially emptied reservoir; the overlying rock loses support and collapses along ring faults, creating a large depression. Later eruptions, lakes or sedimentation may modify the caldera.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the characteristics of a caldera?

options.A: Generally much smaller than a typical volcanic crater
options.B: Generally much larger than a typical volcanic crater, may be several kilometres or more across, and can contain lakes, smaller cones, lava domes or renewed volcanic centres
options.C: Always perfectly circular and empty
options.D: Always formed by explosive excavation only

questions.explanation: A caldera is generally much larger than a typical volcanic crater, may be several kilometres or more across, and can contain lakes, smaller cones, lava domes or renewed volcanic centres.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of calderas?

options.A: Paricutin and Sunset Crater
options.B: Crater Lake in Oregon (caldera of Mount Mazama), Yellowstone in the United States, and Toba in Indonesia
options.C: Mauna Loa and Kilauea
options.D: Mount Fuji and Mount Vesuvius

questions.explanation: Crater Lake in Oregon occupies the caldera of Mount Mazama; Yellowstone in the United States has large caldera systems; Toba in Indonesia is another major caldera system.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Can a caldera contain a lake?

options.A: No, calderas are always dry
options.B: Yes; a caldera may fill with rainwater, groundwater or other water sources and form a caldera lake, such as Crater Lake in Oregon
options.C: Only if it is located in Iceland
options.D: Only if it is smaller than a crater

questions.explanation: A caldera may fill with rainwater, groundwater or other water sources and form a caldera lake, such as Crater Lake in Oregon.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes a crater from a caldera?

options.A: A crater is usually much larger than a caldera
options.B: A crater is usually smaller and vent-centred, while a caldera is a much larger collapse depression
options.C: Both are formed only by explosive excavation
options.D: A caldera is always bowl-shaped and small

questions.explanation: A crater is usually smaller and vent-centred; a caldera is a much larger collapse depression.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a lava dome?

options.A: A broad, gently sloping dome built of fluid basaltic lava
options.B: A steep-sided mound formed when very viscous lava is extruded slowly and accumulates near a vent rather than flowing far away; dome collapse can generate dangerous pyroclastic flows
options.C: A large collapse depression formed after magma withdrawal
options.D: A long crack in the crust from which lava emerges

questions.explanation: A lava dome is a steep-sided mound formed when very viscous lava is extruded slowly and accumulates near a vent rather than flowing far away. Dome collapse can generate dangerous pyroclastic flows.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a volcanic neck or plug?

options.A: A sheet-like intrusive body that cuts across rock layers
options.B: Hardened magma that solidified within a volcanic conduit; after erosion removes the softer surrounding cone, the resistant plug may remain as a prominent landform
options.C: A sheet-like intrusive body emplaced parallel to rock layers
options.D: A very large intrusive body formed at depth

questions.explanation: A volcanic neck or plug is hardened magma that solidified within a volcanic conduit; after erosion removes the softer surrounding cone, the resistant plug may remain as a prominent landform.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a dyke?

options.A: A sheet-like intrusive igneous body emplaced parallel to existing rock layers
options.B: A sheet-like intrusive igneous body that cuts across pre-existing rock layers, commonly occupying a fracture
options.C: A very large intrusive body generally formed at depth
options.D: A steep-sided mound formed by viscous lava

questions.explanation: A dyke is a sheet-like intrusive igneous body that cuts across pre-existing rock layers, commonly occupying a fracture.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a sill?

options.A: A sheet-like intrusive igneous body that cuts across pre-existing rock layers
options.B: A sheet-like intrusive igneous body emplaced parallel to existing rock layers
options.C: A very large intrusive body formed at depth
options.D: Hardened magma that solidified within a volcanic conduit

questions.explanation: A sill is a sheet-like intrusive igneous body emplaced parallel to existing rock layers.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a batholith?

options.A: A small, steep cone made of loose pyroclastic fragments
options.B: A very large intrusive body of igneous rock, generally formed at depth and exposed after long-term uplift and erosion
options.C: A sheet-like intrusive body parallel to rock layers
options.D: A large collapse depression at a volcano

questions.explanation: A batholith is a very large intrusive body of igneous rock, generally formed at depth and exposed after long-term uplift and erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is a volcanic island?

options.A: An island made only of coral
options.B: An island built partly or wholly by volcanic eruptions, either at an oceanic hotspot, a mid-ocean ridge or a volcanic island arc above a subduction zone
options.C: An island formed only by glacial deposition
options.D: An island formed only by river sedimentation

questions.explanation: A volcanic island is an island built partly or wholly by volcanic eruptions, either at an oceanic hotspot, a mid-ocean ridge or a volcanic island arc above a subduction zone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Pacific Ring of Fire?

options.A: A single continuous volcano encircling the Pacific Ocean
options.B: A popular geographical term for the broad belt of frequent earthquakes and volcanic activity around much of the Pacific Ocean basin, associated largely with subduction zones and plate boundaries
options.C: A chain of hotspot volcanoes in the Atlantic Ocean
options.D: A mid-ocean ridge in the Indian Ocean

questions.explanation: The Pacific Ring of Fire is a popular geographical term for the broad belt of frequent earthquakes and volcanic activity around much of the Pacific Ocean basin, associated largely with subduction zones and plate boundaries.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is the Ring of Fire volcanically active?

options.A: Because it lies entirely over a single hotspot
options.B: Because many oceanic plates around the Pacific are subducted beneath neighbouring plates; subduction promotes magma generation and volcanic arcs, while plate interactions also generate frequent earthquakes
options.C: Because it is a continental rift zone
options.D: Because it is located at a divergent boundary only

questions.explanation: Many oceanic plates around the Pacific are subducted beneath neighbouring plates; subduction promotes magma generation and volcanic arcs, while plate interactions also generate frequent earthquakes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which regions form parts of the Ring of Fire?

options.A: The Sahara, the Amazon Basin and the Indo-Gangetic Plain
options.B: The western coasts of North and South America, Alaska and the Aleutian Islands, Kamchatka, Japan, the Philippines, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, Tonga and New Zealand
options.C: The Ural Mountains and the Caspian Sea
options.D: The Congo Basin and the Kalahari Desert

questions.explanation: The western coasts of North and South America, Alaska and the Aleutian Islands, Kamchatka, Japan, the Philippines, Indonesia, Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, Tonga and New Zealand are among the regions associated with the broader Pacific belt.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Is the Ring of Fire a perfect continuous ring of volcanoes?

options.A: Yes, it is a single continuous volcanic structure
options.B: No; it is a popular descriptive term, not a single continuous volcanic structure, and consists of separate volcanic regions and tectonic environments around the Pacific margin
options.C: Yes, and it is caused by one connected magma system
options.D: No; it is a formal scientific region defined by the Smithsonian

questions.explanation: The Ring of Fire is a popular descriptive term, not a single continuous volcanic structure; it consists of separate volcanic regions and tectonic environments around the Pacific margin. The Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program describes it as a popular term rather than a formal scientific region.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Are all volcanoes in the Ring of Fire caused by the same process?

options.A: Yes, all are caused by hotspot volcanism
options.B: No; subduction is the dominant cause in many regions, but tectonic settings and volcanic processes vary around the Pacific, and some nearby volcanic systems may be associated with rifting or other processes
options.C: Yes, all are caused by continental rifting
options.D: Yes, all are caused by a single mantle plume

questions.explanation: Subduction is the dominant cause in many regions, but tectonic settings and volcanic processes vary around the Pacific; some nearby volcanic systems may be associated with rifting or other processes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is the Ring of Fire important?

options.A: It contains no active volcanoes
options.B: It contains a large proportion of the world's active and geologically young volcanoes and is a major global belt of earthquake and tsunami hazard
options.C: It is the only place where volcanoes occur
options.D: It is a single connected magma system

questions.explanation: The Ring of Fire contains a large proportion of the world's active and geologically young volcanoes and is a major global belt of earthquake and tsunami hazard.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are major volcanic regions of the world?

options.A: The Pacific Ring of Fire, the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and Iceland, the Mediterranean volcanic region, the Sunda–Banda arc of Indonesia, the East African Rift and Afar region, the Andes and Central American volcanic arcs, and hotspot regions such as Hawaii and Yellowstone
options.B: Only the Pacific Ring of Fire
options.C: Only the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
options.D: Only hotspot regions

questions.explanation: Major volcanic regions include the Pacific Ring of Fire, the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and Iceland, the Mediterranean volcanic region, the Sunda–Banda arc of Indonesia, the East African Rift and Afar region, the Andes and Central American volcanic arcs, and hotspot regions such as Hawaii and Yellowstone.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are the Andes volcanic?

options.A: Because they lie over a single hotspot
options.B: Because the Nazca Plate and other oceanic plates subduct beneath the South American Plate along the western margin of South America, generating magma and volcanic arcs along the Andes
options.C: Because they lie at a divergent boundary
options.D: Because they are part of a continental rift system

questions.explanation: The Nazca Plate and other oceanic plates subduct beneath the South American Plate along the western margin of South America, generating magma and volcanic arcs along the Andes.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why is Indonesia highly volcanic?

options.A: Because it lies over a single hotspot
options.B: Because it lies within a complex convergent region where the Indo-Australian Plate is subducted beneath parts of the Sunda and other plate systems, producing multiple volcanic arcs
options.C: Because it lies at a divergent boundary
options.D: Because it is part of the East African Rift

questions.explanation: Indonesia lies within a complex convergent region where the Indo-Australian Plate is subducted beneath parts of the Sunda and other plate systems, producing multiple volcanic arcs.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why does Iceland have frequent volcanic activity?

options.A: Because it lies only at a convergent boundary
options.B: Because it lies astride the divergent Mid-Atlantic Ridge and is also influenced by a hotspot or mantle plume, a combination that supports repeated magma generation and eruptions
options.C: Because it lies only over a subduction zone
options.D: Because it is part of the East African Rift

questions.explanation: Iceland lies astride the divergent Mid-Atlantic Ridge and is also influenced by a hotspot or mantle plume; this combination supports repeated magma generation and eruptions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are volcanoes found in East Africa?

options.A: Because of subduction of the Indo-Australian Plate
options.B: Because the East African Rift is a continental rifting system where the lithosphere is being stretched and thinned; decompression melting and related mantle processes produce volcanic activity
options.C: Because of a single hotspot only
options.D: Because of a convergent boundary only

questions.explanation: The East African Rift is a continental rifting system where the lithosphere is being stretched and thinned; decompression melting and related mantle processes produce volcanic activity.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Are all volcanic regions associated with subduction?

options.A: Yes, all volcanic regions are associated with subduction
options.B: No; volcanoes also occur at divergent boundaries, continental rifts and intraplate hotspots
options.C: No; volcanoes occur only at hotspots
options.D: Yes, but only in the Pacific

questions.explanation: Not all volcanic regions are associated with subduction; volcanoes also occur at divergent boundaries, continental rifts and intraplate hotspots.

questions.question: What are the Deccan Traps?

options.A: A currently active composite volcano in the Andaman Sea
options.B: An enormous flood-basalt province in western and central India formed by extensive fissure-fed volcanic eruptions near the end of the Cretaceous Period; ancient volcanic rocks, not a currently active volcano
options.C: A small cinder cone in Karnataka
options.D: A large caldera lake in Maharashtra

questions.explanation: The Deccan Traps are an enormous flood-basalt province in western and central India, formed by extensive fissure-fed volcanic eruptions near the end of the Cretaceous Period; they are ancient volcanic rocks, not a currently active volcano.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Volcanoes and Volcanic Features of India
questions.question: Why are the Deccan Traps called 'Traps'?

options.A: Because they trap volcanic gases
options.B: The word comes from a term meaning stairs, referring to the step-like landscape formed by successive layers of basalt lava flows and their differential erosion
options.C: Because they are located in a trapdoor fault zone
options.D: Because they contain trapped fossils

questions.explanation: The word 'trap' comes from a term meaning stairs, referring to the step-like landscape formed by successive layers of basalt lava flows and their differential erosion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.chapter: Volcanoes and Volcanic Features of India
questions.question: Which statement about volcanic features in India is correct?

options.A: India has no ancient volcanic rocks
options.B: India contains ancient volcanic rocks and intrusive igneous bodies in several regions; the Deccan Traps are the best-known flood-basalt province, while Barren Island is the key example of a historically active volcano
options.C: Barren Island is a flood-basalt province
options.D: The Deccan Traps are India's only active volcano

questions.explanation: India contains ancient volcanic rocks and intrusive igneous bodies in several regions; the Deccan Traps are the best-known flood-basalt province, while Barren Island is the key example of a historically active volcano.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main hazards of volcanic eruptions?

options.A: Only lava flows
options.B: Lava flows, ash fall, pyroclastic flows, lahars, volcanic gases, ballistic projectiles, landslides or sector collapse, volcanic earthquakes, tsunamis in some settings, and disruption to aviation and infrastructure
options.C: Only ash fall and lahars
options.D: Only volcanic gases

questions.explanation: The main hazards include lava flows, ash fall, pyroclastic flows, lahars, volcanic gases, ballistic projectiles, landslides or sector collapse, volcanic earthquakes, tsunamis in some settings and disruption to aviation and infrastructure.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is the danger from volcanic ash?

options.A: It is harmless and beneficial
options.B: Ash can cause respiratory irritation, reduce visibility, damage engines and machinery, contaminate water supplies, overload roofs when wet and disrupt aviation
options.C: It only affects plants
options.D: It only causes skin burns

questions.explanation: Ash can cause respiratory irritation, reduce visibility, damage engines and machinery, contaminate water supplies, overload roofs when wet and disrupt aviation.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are pyroclastic flows especially dangerous?

options.A: Because they move very slowly
options.B: Because they are fast-moving and extremely hot mixtures of gas, ash and rock that can travel rapidly down slopes and across valleys, causing severe burns, asphyxiation and destruction
options.C: Because they only occur underwater
options.D: Because they are cold and harmless

questions.explanation: Pyroclastic flows are fast-moving and extremely hot mixtures of gas, ash and rock that can travel rapidly down slopes and across valleys, causing severe burns, asphyxiation and destruction.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What are the benefits of volcanic regions?

options.A: Only tourism
options.B: Volcanic soils can become fertile after weathering; geothermal energy can be harnessed; volcanic landscapes attract tourism; eruptions create new land; and volcanic rocks and minerals provide construction materials and resources
options.C: Only geothermal energy
options.D: Only new land creation

questions.explanation: Benefits include fertile volcanic soils after weathering, geothermal energy, tourism, creation of new land, and volcanic rocks and minerals as construction materials and resources.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Are volcanic soils always fertile immediately after an eruption?

options.A: Yes, always
options.B: No; fresh lava and ash may initially be barren or harmful, and soil development and nutrient availability take time and depend on climate, rock composition, weathering and ecological recovery
options.C: Yes, but only for one year
options.D: No; volcanic soils are never fertile

questions.explanation: Fresh lava and ash may initially be barren or harmful; soil development and nutrient availability take time and depend on climate, rock composition, weathering and ecological recovery.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: What is geothermal energy?

options.A: Energy from burning volcanic rocks
options.B: Heat from within Earth that can be used directly or to generate electricity, especially in regions with high subsurface temperatures and accessible geothermal fluids
options.C: Energy from volcanic gases
options.D: Energy from solar radiation on volcanoes

questions.explanation: Geothermal energy is heat from within Earth that can be used directly or to generate electricity, especially in regions with high subsurface temperatures and accessible geothermal fluids.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes magma and lava?

options.A: Magma is molten rock at the surface; lava is molten rock below the surface
options.B: Magma is molten or partially molten rock below the surface; lava is magma erupted onto the surface
options.C: Magma and lava are identical
options.D: Lava is found only in space

questions.explanation: Magma is molten or partially molten rock below the surface; lava is magma erupted onto the surface.

questions.subject: General Knowledge

options.B: Volcanic ash is fine rock and glass fragments, not ash from combustion
options.C: Volcanic ash is always larger than 64 mm
options.D: Volcanic ash is a type of lava flow

questions.explanation: Volcanic ash is fine rock and glass fragments, not ash from combustion.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Why are shield volcanoes broad and gently sloping?

options.A: Because they are built of viscous rhyolitic lava
options.B: Because fluid lava spreads widely
options.C: Because they are formed by caldera collapse
options.D: Because they are made only of ash

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about composite volcanoes is correct?

options.A: They are built only of fluid lava flows
options.B: They are built from alternating lava and pyroclastic layers and can have explosive eruptions
options.C: They are always small cinder cones
options.D: They are formed only by fissure eruptions

questions.explanation: Composite volcanoes are built from alternating lava and pyroclastic layers and can have explosive eruptions.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about cinder cones is correct?

options.A: They are generally larger than shield volcanoes
options.B: They are generally smaller, steep-sided cones made largely of loose pyroclastic fragments
options.C: They are built of alternating lava and ash layers
options.D: They are large collapse depressions

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about fissure eruptions is correct?

options.A: Fissure eruption is simply another name for a shield volcano

options.C: Fissure eruptions occur only at hotspots
options.D: Fissure eruptions form only cinder cones

questions.explanation: Fissure eruption refers to lava emerging along cracks; it is not simply another name for a shield volcano.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement correctly compares a crater and a caldera?

options.A: A crater is usually larger than a caldera
options.B: A crater is usually smaller and vent-centred; a caldera is a much larger collapse depression
options.C: Both are formed only by explosive excavation
options.D: A caldera is always a small bowl-shaped depression

questions.explanation: A crater is usually smaller and vent-centred; a caldera is a much larger collapse depression.

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about active, dormant and extinct volcano categories is correct?

options.A: They have a single universal time threshold
options.B: They have no single universal time threshold
options.C: They are based only on colour
options.D: They are based only on height

questions.question: Which statement about the Ring of Fire is correct?

options.C: It is a single connected magma system

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about volcano locations is correct?

options.D: No volcanoes occur at plate boundaries

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about subduction-related, rift and hotspot volcanoes is correct?

options.C: Rift volcanoes form only at subduction zones
options.D: Hotspot volcanoes form only at divergent boundaries

questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.question: Which statement about India's volcanic features is correct?

questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.question: Which of the following best defines volcanic activity and its major causes?

questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes active, dormant and extinct volcanoes?
